title: AWS: a nightly read refused at the key, and classic clusters that stopped starting
synthetic: Fictional teaching case for Cinderline Components. Names, addresses, account and project identifiers and every error text are invented; nothing was deployed or observed. Hostnames ending in .example stand in for the regional names on the current AWS pages; 111122223333 is a placeholder account ID.

vpc-cinderline-dbx (10.0.0.0/16); compute subnets subnet-compute-a (10.0.32.0/20) and subnet-compute-b (10.0.48.0/20); interface endpoints in subnet-endpoints (10.0.8.0/24): vpce-relay 10.0.8.21 and vpce-rest 10.0.8.22

evidence.capture: The exact error or symptom text, its time, the run or cluster ID, and which service answered (or that none did)
evidence.where: The job run or cluster event log
evidence.doesNotProve: Which layer is at fault until the service that answered, if any, has been named

evidence.capture: The job's run-as principal as its settings show it
evidence.doesNotProve: That the principal holds any privilege, or anything about the network

evidence.capture: SHOW GRANTS on the catalog, the schema and the table, read for the acting principal and its groups
evidence.doesNotProve: Anything about storage permissions or reachability

evidence.capture: The storage credential's IAM role ARN and account, and the external location that resolved for the path
evidence.where: Unity Catalog storage credential and external location
evidence.doesNotProve: That any policy admits the role on the prefix

evidence.capture: The role's permissions policy statements for the bucket and prefix
evidence.doesNotProve: What the bucket policy or the key policy say

evidence.capture: The bucket policy's statements for the exact role ARN
evidence.doesNotProve: Whether the key policy lets the role decrypt

evidence.capture: The key policy statements and grants naming the exact role ARN, and the key's region and state
evidence.doesNotProve: Whether the network path to the key or the bucket exists

evidence.capture: Which instance profile the cluster launched with, and its role ARN
evidence.doesNotProve: Anything about reads that go through Unity Catalog

evidence.capture: The relay hostname's answer resolved from an instance in subnet-compute-a, with time
evidence.where: An instance in the compute subnet
evidence.doesNotProve: That a route or security group admits the traffic

evidence.capture: The private hosted zone's records and its associated VPCs
The route table associated with the compute subnet
evidence.doesNotProve: That a security group admits the flow

evidence.capture: Outbound rules of the nodes' security group
evidence.doesNotProve: What the endpoint's own security group admits

evidence.capture: Inbound rules of the endpoints' security group against the current compute ranges
evidence.doesNotProve: Endpoint registration or anything about permissions

evidence.capture: VPC flow log REJECT records at the endpoint's network interface for the failure time
evidence.doesNotProve: Which rule to change; only that packets were refused there

evidence.capture: The endpoint's state and its registration in the workspace's network configuration
evidence.where: VPC endpoint vpce-relay and the account console

symptoms.title: The nightly job is refused after the catalog agreed
symptoms.observed: AccessDenied (KMS): the assumed role cinderline-lake-cred-role is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on alias/cinderline-lake
symptoms.context: The bucket's objects moved to SSE-KMS under alias/cinderline-lake last week. Ana still reads the same prefix from legacy-interactive without trouble. Unity Catalog raised no PERMISSION_DENIED.

symptoms.title: Classic clusters stopped starting
symptoms.observed: Cluster start failed after a bootstrap timeout reaching the secure cluster connectivity relay; no service returned an error
symptoms.context: On Monday the compute subnets moved from 10.0.16.0/20 to 10.0.32.0/20 and 10.0.48.0/20. No job, grant or credential changed.
